title: Conditional Poincare-before-Duhamel shell transport
question: Can the nonnegative Doob shell variance from R-398 be converted, shell by shell, into a conditional Dirichlet energy divided by a measurable birth-death spectral gap, thereby replacing the unresolved direct shell bound by two separately testable inputs?

new_perspective.principle: Poincare before Duhamel: control each conditional likelihood fluctuation before any real-time product estimate.
route: For each oriented collar prefix a and next coordinate k, form the reference conditional law pi_a(k)=p(a,k)/p(a) and the conditional likelihood f_a(k)=q(a,k)/p(a,k).
Put a reversible nearest-neighbour birth-death form on the ordered finite coordinate levels with conductance c_a(k)=min(pi_a(k),pi_a(k+1)); compute its first nonzero generalized eigenvalue lambda_a.

Use the exact conditional Poincare inequality Var_pi(f)<=Dirichlet_pi(f)/lambda_a and sum over prefix parents. The R-398 shell energy is the left side; the right side is a local discrete gradient budget.

A uniform positive lambda_a together with a source-, volume-, cutoff- and shape-uniform exponential gradient estimate would give the required weighted shell summability without commuting growing Hamiltonian powers through every bond.

Stress both orientations, every history prefix, source signs and supports, beta values and the full R-398 volume/cutoff grid; retain the minimum conditional gap and the Poincare slack instead of inferring uniformity from a finite minimum.
new_perspective.qft_bridge: The route offers a conditional-information-to-Dirichlet interface for the folded two-replica collar. It does not itself provide the conditional gap, gradient decay, common form core, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction or a physical gap.

finite_theorem.spectral_gap: lambda_a is the second eigenvalue of diag(pi_a)^(-1/2) L_a diag(pi_a)^(-1/2), with L_a the conductance Laplacian
finite_theorem.analytic_split: Uniform shell control is split into a conditional-gap theorem and a gradient-decay theorem; finite lambda minima are diagnostics only.

lean_crosscheck.boundary: Lean checks finite scalar variance/Dirichlet algebra and the weighted transfer skeleton only; it does not formalize Q3 spectra, conditional-gap uniformity, gradient decay, common cores or QFT limits.

promotion_criteria: Prove a phase-conditioned conditional spectral-gap lower bound for the same birth-death or physically derived local Dirichlet form, uniform in source, volume, cutoff and allowed shapes.
Prove a matching gradient-decay estimate for the actual folded or Doob likelihood on a Hamiltonian-derived common core, in both orientations and adjoints.
Sum the weighted shell transfer with rho>mu/4 and then pass cutoff and exhaustion limits before invoking common-alpha or OS/KMS interfaces.
stop_conditions: If the conditional gap collapses under a validated increasing-cutoff or phase-boundary stress, keep the shell decomposition but register conditional Poincare as a route-local obstruction.
If the gap survives but the likelihood gradient grows with shell radius, redirect to a Euclidean transfer or polymer estimate rather than claiming shell summability.
If a uniform gap and gradient theorem require global uniqueness, restrict the route to within-phase boundary-conditioned statements and retain phase coexistence as open.
boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite conditional Poincare and shell-gradient diagnostic. It proves no cutoff/volume/source/shape-uniform gap, no gradient decay theorem, no common form core, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction, mass gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A or Pre-A closure.
no_overclaim: The finite Poincare inequality is an exact change of bookkeeping. A positive finite minimum gap is not a thermodynamic lower bound, and the gradient profile is not a real-time Lieb-Robinson estimate.
